subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw solve browser-heavy channel starvation with first-class browser/per-channel lane routing, fold it into broader per-agent lane work, or choose a priority/reserve scheduler policy instead?
rationale: The code primitives exist, but exposing routing changes public config, fairness guarantees, and resource-cap behavior across channels and upgrades.

options.title: Design workload lane routing
options.body: Add a server-owned, validated lane-routing model for browser/channel/agent classification with aggregate caps, compatibility defaults, docs, and tests.

options.title: Fold into per-agent lanes
options.body: Treat browser starvation as a use case of the broader per-agent command-lane issue and avoid per-channel/browser config unless per-agent isolation proves insufficient.

options.title: Prefer priority fairness
options.body: Avoid new lane config for now and pursue foreground reserves or aging so fast user turns remain responsive on the shared lane.

recommendation.title: Design workload lane routing
recommendation.body: Add a server-owned, validated lane-routing model for browser/channel/agent classification with aggregate caps, compatibility defaults, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for command-lane concurrency and current scheduler policy points to this person.
